prOriginal.nota: Upstream calcom/cal.com now redirects to calcom/cal.diy. Found by head branch fix-collective-events-have-only-one-team-attendee-on-the-google-event-7754-cal-1267; benchmark head de62829 is the PR's last commit and squash c4e5d168 has the same 22-file diff (only unrelated main-merge drift in imports). Files later moved: EventManager -> packages/features/bookings/lib, CalendarManager -> packages/features/calendars/lib, handleNewBooking -> service/RegularBookingService + handleNewBooking/loadUsers.

fix-handle-collective-multiple-host-on-d.reason: PR #11733 'fix: Backwards compatibility on google reschedule/cancel' (body: fixes issue introduced in #10967) replaced the dead `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : destinationCalendar.find(cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` in updateEvent and deleteEvent with `(externalCalendarId ? find(...) : undefined) || 'primary'`, so update no longer receives an undefined calendarId. It falls back to primary rather than restoring the destination-calendar externalId; today's code keeps that shape.

astra.pergunta: Is #03 confirmado by #11733 (dead lookup removed, undefined calendarId replaced by primary) or pendente because the old fallback to destinationCalendar.externalId was not restored?
astra.resposta: Confirmado under 'any fix counts': #11733 removes the falsy lookup and update now gets 'primary' instead of undefined; it does not restore the destination-calendar fallback, which limits coverage but does not make it pendente; not descontinuado since it was a targeted fix.

fix-handle-collective-multiple-host-on-d.reason: In create.handler.ts, PR #11267 (feat: autolink org on provider signup) changed `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` back to `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, restoring the original condition so billing-disabled orgs get a slug again. The handler file was later moved/removed from the upstream tree.

PR #11327 'fix: Duplicate calendar events' changed Office365 createEvent to `createEvent(event, credentialId)` selecting `destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId) ?? destinationCalendar[0]`; Lark got the same pattern. Today both Office365 and Lark createEvent accept credentialId and pick the matching destination.

EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents (now packages/features/bookings/lib/EventManager.ts) still resolves credential from calendarCredentials then CredentialRepository and calls `updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calendarExternalId)` unconditionally even if none was found. CalendarManager.updateEvent (packages/features/calendars/lib/CalendarManager.ts) still dereferences credential.appName/credential.type in its return.

PR #11574 'fix: Booking failures when there are no destination calendars but Google Meet location' (possible regression from #10967) changed the check to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`. Today's EventManager still uses the optional chaining.

PR #19459 (refactor: event type builder) replaced `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` with `withDestinationCalendar([...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars])`, so a null organizer destination no longer drops the other hosts' calendars. Today RegularBookingService uses the same `[...(destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

PR #14272 (refactor: Introduce crmManager) changed the reference mapping in EventManager.create from `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` to `credentialId: result?.credentialId || undefined`, so video references keep their credentialId again. Today it is `...getCredentialPayload(result)` which keeps any positive credentialId regardless of type.

EventManager.updateLocation today still builds referencesToCreate with `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and credentialId from result.credentialId, while CalendarManager.updateEvent still returns neither externalId nor credentialId. editLocation.handler still persists these references via updateLocationById.

The per-reference loop with the recurring branch over organizer credentials and `updBooking.references.find(first _calendar ref)` survived #12651 as a fallback, then PR #14261 (chore: EventManager add cancelEvent method, part of a CRM refactor) deleted it. Today EventManager.deleteEventsAndMeetings deletes each calendar reference once with its own credential, using thirdPartyRecurringEventId for series.

astra.pergunta: Recurring cancel loop (per reference x organizer credentials x first ref of each booking) was deleted by #14261 (chore: EventManager cancelEvent) and replaced by per-reference deletion with each reference's own credential. Descontinuado or confirmado for #13 and sncc-01?
astra.resposta: Both descontinuado via #14261: the refactor removed the path that picked only the first reference per booking and the bookings x credentials batch inside the reference loop; no evidence of a change targeting the bug. #12651 kept both problems in its fallback.

fix-handle-collective-multiple-host-on-d.reason: Google createEvent today selects `externalCalendarId ?? (destinationCalendar.find(cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId || 'primary')`, but CalendarManager.createEvent passes externalCalendarId only for delegation credentials. For credential-less destinations EventManager still calls `createEvent(firstCalendarCredential, event)`, so the find fails and the event goes to primary.

The credential-less branch of EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents still calls `createEvent(firstCalendarCredential, event)` without destination.externalId; CalendarManager.createEvent still returns `externalId` from its argument, and references are still built with `externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined`.

The recurring deletion batch (remaining bookings x organizer calendar credentials) nested inside the loop over calendar references was removed wholesale by PR #14261, a refactor moving cancellation into EventManager.cancelEvent. Today each calendar reference is deleted exactly once, so the repetition no longer exists.

astra.pergunta: Recurring cancel loop (per reference x organizer credentials x first ref of each booking) was deleted by #14261 (chore: EventManager cancelEvent) and replaced by per-reference deletion with each reference's own credential. Descontinuado or confirmado for #13 and sncc-01?
astra.resposta: Both descontinuado via #14261: the refactor removed the path that picked only the first reference per booking and the bookings x credentials batch inside the reference loop; no evidence of a change targeting the bug. #12651 kept both problems in its fallback.

fix-handle-collective-multiple-host-on-d.reason: loadUsers moved to packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/loadUsers.ts but its catch still does `if (error instanceof HttpError || error instanceof Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError) throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: error.message })`, forwarding the raw Prisma message to the client.

loadDynamicUsers in today's loadUsers.ts still throws a plain `new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")`, and the loadUsers catch still maps non-HttpError/non-Prisma errors to HttpError 500 'Unable to load users'.

computeTeamData in RegularBookingService still pushes `{...user.destinationCalendar, externalId}` for COLLECTIVE members into the event's destinationCalendar, webhookData still starts with `...evt`, and handleWebhookTrigger/sendPayload still serialize the data unfiltered (`payload: data`).
